comment: Drift that already existed when scripts/check-publish-drift.mjs landed (core#129).
Each waiver is pinned to an exact { name, version, fingerprint }, where the
fingerprint covers both the published tarball and the local packed tree. It
therefore waives one measured state and nothing else: bump the package, or let
its content move again, and the waiver stops matching and the guard fails. A
waiver on a package that is no longer drifting also fails, so these get deleted
rather than accumulated. This file is not a place to silence new findings.
Regenerate a fingerprint with: node scripts/check-publish-drift.mjs --json
